BGEO.notes: Diluted EPS in Georgian lari (GEL), from the company's 3Q26/9M26 results announcement (PDF copy of the release hosted on directorstalkinterviews.com; I read the document itself, but it is not on the company's site or an exchange site - lionfinancegroup.uk was blocked - so re-check 'primary' if strict). Basic EPS: 9M 43.81 vs 36.45 (+20.2%), Q3 15.57 vs 12.75 (+22.1%). Profit attributable: 9M 1,865.7 vs 1,571.6 (+18.7%), Q3 661.9 vs 547.2 (+21.0%). CAUTION: the changes are nominal in GEL; the company expects 2026 average inflation of 5.3% in Georgia and 4.5% in Armenia, and the GEL/GBP rate also moves - the script will deflate with UK inflation. No EPS or profit guidance exists: only medium-term targets (loan growth c.15% a year, ROAE 20%+, payout 30-50%), which are not earnings guidance, so 'guidance' is null. Note that both targets are below current run-rates (loan growth 24.6% c.c., ROAE 27.2%). No adjusted figures for 2026 (company reports no one-offs in 9M26 or 9M25). Nothing departed: no exited business or country found. Comparison-base remarks: renegotiated payment-system terms gave a high fee base in 4Q25; AFS 2025 opex included a retention bonus (ex-bonus AFS profit growth would be 28.0% in 9M26 instead of the reported 43%). Dividend yield exists in the source (2.71%), so 'dividend' is null; declared quarterly dividends: 4Q25 2.75, 1Q26 2.85, 2Q26 3.05, 3Q26 3.25 GEL.

SNWS.notes: All figures read in the 4 Nov 2026 preliminary results RNS (full text on ticker.app) and the 6 May 2026 interim RNS. Statutory basic EPS FY2026 10.1p vs 11.7p = -13.7%. Second half by subtraction (my arithmetic): 10.1-5.0 = 5.1p vs 11.7-5.6 = 6.1p = -16.4%. Adjusted basic EPS: year 11.3 vs 11.1 = +1.8% (company states +1.8%); second half by subtraction 11.3-5.2 = 6.1 vs 11.1-5.4 = 5.7 = +7.0% (my arithmetic, rounded inputs). GUIDANCE: none usable. The company says only that there 'will be a short-term impact on profitability for the business in FY2027', with 7-9m pounds of early-life transition costs in FY2027 and 21-27m of implementation cost split equally between adjusting items and capex; no EPS or profit figure. Broker forecast seen on Stockopedia (Canaccord FY27E adjusted EPS 7.3p, cut 27.7% from 10.1p) is an analyst estimate, not counted. PERMANENT: not applied. Print decline is structural (newspaper revenue -4.1%, magazines -3.2%; company's planning assumption -3% to -5% a year), but it is a revenue trend the company has offset: adjusted operating profit 38.7m vs 39.1m, contracts extended to 2036-2037 with new territories (+c.375m revenue a year). The statutory profit fall is explained by one-off items, not by a lasting cause. DEPARTED: nothing lost; no contract loss found. Source dividend yield exists (5.65p ordinary; no special this year vs 3.00p last year).
